claims.text: A tailored short-to-medium annealing treatment can induce a controlled amount of short-range order in a primarily FCC CrCoNi-based alloy.
Annealing-induced short-range order will simultaneously enhance yield strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
Conventionally hot-rolled or cast, single-phase equiatomic or near-equiatomic FCC alloys can have minimal pre-existing short-range order.
A moderate-temperature anneal of calibrated duration can increase short-range order without causing phase decomposition.
There is a narrow temperature-time window in which short-range order is enhanced without overaging or formation of deleterious secondary phases.
The proposed treatment is expected to work mainly for predominantly FCC high-entropy alloys.
The treatment may fail in an already multiphase microstructure or when annealing exceeds the optimal range.
Induced short-range order creates nanoscale regions of enhanced lattice distortion.
The short-range-ordered regions impede dislocation motion.
Short-range order promotes deformation twinning or transformation-induced plasticity at stress concentrations near crack tips.
Short-range order increases local bonding strength.
Impeded dislocation glide caused by short-range order raises yield strength.
Controlled strain-induced transformations absorb deformation energy and thereby improve ductility and fracture resistance.
Enhanced local bonding strength caused by short-range order increases Young’s modulus.
Optimized annealing is expected to increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated alloy.
Optimized annealing is expected to increase elongation by approximately 20% relative to the untreated alloy.
Optimized annealing is expected to elevate Young’s modulus and improve fracture toughness relative to the untreated alloy.
An as-rolled or conventionally processed CrCoNi alloy can have a yield strength around 350 MPa.
Excessive ordering or annealing-induced brittle secondary phases will eliminate the proposed mechanical-property benefits.
The optimal annealing parameters and property improvements depend on alloy composition and may also depend on grain size and other microstructural factors.
